summary: Two summer journeys in the far north of Europe by Edward Rae and a friend he calls “the Doctor”, written up from his journals. In 1873 they sailed from Hull to Norway and up the coast by Throndhjem and the Lôfoden Islands to Tromsö, crossed the fjelds of Norwegian Lapland by Kauto-keino with Lapp guides, came down the Muônio and Torneå rivers by boat to Haparanda, and went home through Sweden by Upsala, Stockholm, and Gotland. In 1874 they sailed round the North Cape to Archangel, went up the Dvina and the Pînega, crossed by the Kûloi river to Mezén, and travelled among the Samoyedes of the Kânin peninsula, returning by the White Sea and the Solovetsk monastery. Rae writes about the people they met, their tents, reindeer, food and travel, mosquitoes and weather, with a short Samoyede vocabulary. Three plates, a title vignette, and a map of the routes.
